Title: Missing GPIO_AF7_USART3

Body:
When creating a project with CubeMX and the STM32C092RCTx and want to put USART3_TX on PC14, CubeMX will generate a project which can't be compiled. The issue is that the definition of GPIO_AF7_USART3 is missing in stm32c0xx_hal_gpio_ex.h.

I have created a pull request which solves the issue:
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32c0xx-hal-driver/pull/7

Title: register keyword incompatible with C++17

Body:
There were similar issues found and fixed for the H7 and F4 code bases, but wanted to raise this simple fix for preventing future compiler issues for everyone.

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/issues/15

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/issues/27

The issue is that the register keyword was depreciated in C++11 and removed in C++17 because the intent of the keyword no longer makes sense with modern compilers capabilities. 

Specific changes need, remove register keyword on the following lines (potentially more, but this is what my compiler hit as definite errors):
stm32c0xx_ll_adc.h:4010
stm32c0xx_ll_adc.h:4115
stm32c0xx_ll_adc.h:4120
stm32c0xx_ll_rtc.h:1077
stm32c0xx_ll_rtc.h:1105
stm32c0xx_ll_rtc.h:1410
stm32c0xx_ll_rtc.h:1438
stm32c0xx_ll_rtc.h:1741

Title: STM32C051xx  missing GPIO_AF0_USART2 definition

Body:
According to datasheet DS14721 Rev 2, PD3 can have USART2_CTS/USART2_NSS with AF0 but HAL GPIO does not define it for this part number:

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32c0xx-hal-driver/blob/c283b143bef6bdaacf64240ee6f15eb61dad6125/Inc/stm32c0xx_hal_gpio_ex.h#L64-L66


Proposed patch:
patch
- #if defined(STM32C031xx) || defined(STM32C071xx) || defined(STM32C091xx)  || defined(STM32C092xx) 
+ #if defined(STM32C031xx) || defined(STM32C051xx) || defined(STM32C071xx) || defined(STM32C091xx)  || defined(STM32C092xx) 
 #define GPIO_AF0_USART2        ((uint8_t)0x00)  /*!< USART2 Alternate Function mapping */ 
- #endif /* STM32C031xx | STM32C071xx | STM32C091xx | STM32C092xx*/ 
+ #endif /* STM32C031xx | STM32C051xx | STM32C071xx | STM32C091xx | STM32C092xx*/ 



[IMAGE ATTACHED]

Issue reported by @nessotrin in a PR:
https://github.com/stm32duino/Arduino_Core_STM32/pull/2791

issue_title: Incorrect Alternate Function Mapping for FDCAN
clean_text:
Title: Incorrect Alternate Function Mapping for FDCAN

Body:
When testing the FDCAN on the STM32C092FCP6 with PB8 (Rx) and PC14 (Tx), we discovered that the alternate function mapping in the stm32c0xx_hal_gpio_ex.h definitions is incorrect.  
According to DS14720 Rev. 2, the alternate function mapping for PC14 should be AF13. However, in the definitions, AF13 is assigned to TIM3 and TIM14.  

Additionally, in STM32CubeIDE (v1.19) the code generator selected AF15 for PC14 in the stm32c0xx_hal_msp.c file, which is used for EVENTOUT.

Title: Clarification about DMAMUX tim14_trgo

Body:
I'm not sure if this is a bug, but I stumbled upon this and it looks a bit odd to me:
The C0  RM0490 Rev 5 Table 50/51 list the DMAMUX trigger inputs and synchronization inputs.
In Table 50 (assignment of trigger inputs to resources) _tim14_trgo_ is assigned to Trigger Input **22**, whereas in Table 51 (assignment of synchronization inputs to resources) it is assigned to Sync Input **21**.  
All other mappings are consistent between trigger inputs and synchronization inputs. Therefore I'm wondering, if the _tim14_trgo_ entry in Table 51 might be wrong. (Should it be assigned to **22**?)  

AN5969 section 5.16 says:
> When the same peripherals are available on both products, their DMA assignment of multiplexer inputs to resources, trigger inputs to resources, and synchronization inputs to resources are identical.  

But in the G0 series (RM0444 Rev 6) _TIM14_OC_ is mapped to Input **22** both for Trigger and Sync Input.  
So, the AN5969 section 5.16 statement would be wrong, if on the C0 family _tim14_trgo_ really is mapped to synchronization input 21.

I also checked the definition here in the HAL: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32c0xx-hal-driver/blob/main/Inc/stm32c0xx_ll_dmamux.h#L250  
This definition is **21** in accordance with RM0490. So, if the RM is wrong about the _tim14_trgo_ sync assignment, the HAL definition would also be wrong.  

Could you check, if the _tim14_trgo_ assignment in RM0490 really is correct?

(I did not encounter this by debugging a firmware. I read RM0490 for an opensource firmware library and it just seemed odd.)
